newsitem.title: USA: US marketers wary of lawmakers' heating oil pleas.
newsitem.headline: US marketers wary of lawmakers' heating oil pleas.

text.p: Petroleum marketers plan to meet next week to discuss their outlook for heating oil supplies, amid growing concern among lawmakers that stocks are too low to prevent a price spike this winter.

Twenty one senators and 20 Representatives from Northeastern and Midwestern states sent a letter Wednesday to Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary asking whether the government could sell crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to raise money to buy heating oil for future sales in order to help stem a steep price jump.
While marketers are concerned enough to hold an unscheduled meeting, a senior official at the Petroleum Marketers Association of America said the lawmakers' pleas might be counterproductive.

"A simple analysis of the issue suggests if you put the government in the business of buying heating oil right now, it would have the exact opposite effects that the sponsors intend," said PMAA executive vice president Phillip Chisholm.
"It will drive prices higher," he said.

If the government buys heating oil now to sell later in the event of a shortage, "private entitites will begin to question whether they should build inventory, because they don't know when the government might put that fuel back into the market," he added.

Weekly reports by the Energy Information Administration and American Petroleum Institute show refiners' distillate inventories -- made up of heating oil and diesel -- hovering 15 percent below five-year averages for this time of year.
The marketers will be discussing their outlook for stock levels at the retail level next week, Chisholm said.
Senior Energy Department officials have said they are monitoring heating oil stocks, but do not want to interfere with the market.
There is some question whether the administration will even be able to sell oil from the SPR after September 30, with Congress yet to reauthorize the law governing use of the emergency stockpile.
